Update 2055 IST - Great news! Good news is that the rain has stopped for now but it's still overcast out there. Rain had been coming down the whole night and outfield is still wet which is delaying the start. We'll have to wait and see how it pans out.

Welcome everyone! Day 3 again was dominated by India with their vice captain scoring a century.  But to everyone's disappointment, the moment India declared with a lead of 304 runs, the rain started pouring and it was called a day just before the end of the second session.
... DAY 4, SESSION 1...

The Indian team will be hurt they couldn't bowl today as the rain gods had the final laugh. Tomorrow it will be an early start at 2000 IST to compensate for today's lost overs. Do join us for Day 4 and we hope the weather stays healthy and playable. Adios, take care and goodbye!

The day was purely in favour of India as they extended their lead close to 300. The showman was Ajinkya Rahane who got to his 7th Test hundred with good support from his teammates. Roston Chase was a mere success in terms of a milestone with his maiden 5-fer. Apart from that, West Indies have a great task to climb as they have a mammoth lead to surpass before they set a target for the visiting side.

Finally the hide and seek game of rain has paved its way. The rains have taken the majority of time and kept the players busy going on and off the field post Lunch. With only an hour left in the day, it was decided by the match officials to call it a day. A gist of today's play to follow...

0330 IST UPDATE - The inevitable has happened, folks! The rain though eased off but the conditions haven't improved and the umpires after doing the inspections have come to the conclusion that THEY SHOULD CALL IT A DAY!
0258 IST UPDATE - The rain has stopped finally and the groundstaff are trying their best to clean up the logged water on the outfield. We hope to get some cricketing action pretty soon. Stay tuned.

All we can say is, stay tuned for the latest update.

Right then! A solid batting performance has seen the visitors in a commanding position as they have a mammoth lead of 304 runs. We saw a mini interruption due to rain and the forecast suggests it is not at all good for the remainder of the day and the whole of tomorrow. If you are a West Indies fan, you would want the rain gods to show some mercy. Let's hope for the best. Join us in a bit for the West Indies reply.

With the pitch behaving inconsistently, West Indies will find it difficult to survive against a quality Indian bowling. But before that, they have to pick up 5 Indian wickets. Should they not get that, when will Kohli declare? Lead of 250? 300? Join us tomorrow at 2030 IST (1500 GMT) to find out how Day 3 unfolds. Until then, Adios! Take Care!

The Windies struggled for four hours before things finally started to happen for them in the final session. The pitch started to show some turn and inconsistent bounce, which will only get worse from here on. Shannon Gabriel bowled his heart out and his figures do not justify the way he has bowled. Chase got a couple of important wickets while Bishoo found some grip towards the end.

It seems a pitch difficult for scoring as even the fluent Kohli struggled to get going. Lokesh Rahul was the only one looking settled on the pitch and later in the day, Rahane. Pujara and Kohli got starts but could not convert them as the hosts got a few wickets in the evening session.

34 overs, 99 runs, 3 wickets. A better session for the Windies but a fabulous day for India. They started the day on 126/1, trailing by 70 runs and would have looked to score freely. They could not quite get that but they would be happy with the end result - a lead in excess of 150.

The physio is out in the middle again and early DRINKS have been taken. Rahul is really struggling with his right leg. Might be calf, might be hamstring. Welcome back for the second session. After an attritional opening session, India will be looking to score a bit quicker in this one. The deficit is just 11 and that might get into the lead past 100 by Tea. The players are out in the middle. Shannon Gabriel to start off proceedings after the break to Rahul.
... DAY 2, SESSION 2 ...

The Indian batsmen have played with calmness and authority and seem to be unfazed with the Windies' bowling attack which lacks penetration. The visitors are in the driving seat and look set for a big score. With the deficit just 11 for India, the WI bowlers need to pull up their socks and put in their best efforts otherwise India would pile up a big total and put the West Indies under tremendous pressure. Join us back at 2310 IST for the second session.

Yet another session in India's favour. Scoring has been slow but no wicket was lost. The West Indies bowlers have not been impressive enough and have failed to capitalize on a wicket that was offering something to the quick bowlers and also offering significant turn to the spinners. The quickies haven't hit a proper length and have failed to trouble Rahul and Pujara. The spinners have been either too short or too full and have lacked a sense of rhythm. They need to be more disciplined in order to trouble the well-set pair of Rahul and Pujara and create an opening to get back into the match.

Warm welcome everyone!  Day 1 totally went in India's favour. West Indies were poor with the bat and did not look threatening with the ball at all. For India, Lokesh Rahul is looking good out in the middle and with Virat Kohli and Co. to follow, India are in a position to make a formidable total. Now let's see whether West Indies will make a comeback. Or will India cruise to make this day in their name again? Join us in a bit as we will take you through the proceedings of Day 2.
... Day 2, first session ...

Overall, it was a poor day for West Indies as they failed to put up a good total on the board after opting to bat first and in response, couldn't do justice with the ball too. They will hope to show some stomach  to turn things around tomorrow. On the other hand, can Rahul convert another fifty into a century and provide India with a good lead over the hosts? With a strong middle order, the visiting side will look to repeat their performance of the first Test and be in a commanding position. Do join us tomorrow at 2030 IST. Until then, take care and goodbye!

After getting bowled out for 196, the hosts had to come out and bowl their hearts out. Apart from Gabriel, Cummins and Holder were ineffective as the lines and lengths were easily played off by the visiting side. Chase kept bowling a tight spell from one end but didn't get the required support from his partners. He was the lone wicket taker as he picked up Dhawan's wicket.

That ends the play on day 1. The Indian team have negotiated the final session quite comfortably by scoring 126 runs and trailing by just 70. They started off with a solid opening stand of 87 before Dhawan got out to Chase. Rahul kept on with his shots and scored his maiden fifty where Pujara played a good supporting role by coming in at number 3.

It is 1730 local time and West Indies were trying their best to finish this off but Aleem Dar makes them bowl this one final over...
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Full and outside off, Rahul lunges to defend but misses and is hit on the pads. There is an LBW appeal but the impact is outside off.
Much better, gives this a bit more air, full and outside off, Rahul defends watchfully.
A half tracker again, cut through the covers for a single this time.
A long hop outside off, Pujara punches it in front of point and gets a couple. The deficit is now down to 78. The stand moves to 31 now.
Short and outside off, slapped straight to point.
KRAIGG BRATHWAITE to bowl now.
Full and outside off, well defended.
The batsman works it down the leg side.
On middle, pushed towards mid on.
On middle, Rahul tucks it through square leg and gets a couple.
Full on middle, flicked to deepish mid-wicket for a single.

Ooohh... playing with fire is Pujara with not much time left in the day. He comes down the track but is beaten in the flight. The ball spins in, takes the inside edge, goes onto the pads and goes to backward square leg. Does not carry.
Full and outside off, Pujara flicks it through wide mid on. Marlon Samuels, yes Marlon Samuels dives to his right and half-stops it. A single taken.
Full and outside off, defended watchfully.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
This is wide outside off, Pujara would not have connected even if he had thrown his bat at it. Lucky not to be called a wide.
Full and outside off, pushed straight to cover.
The light seems to have gone down there. However, the umpires do not seem to be too concerned.
On a good length outside off, left alone.
Full and outside off, well blocked out.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
TOP EDGE, SAFE! Full and around off, Rahul looks to sweep but gets a top edge which does not carry to short fine leg where Holder runs to his right.
Slips this down the leg side, left alone.
Short and outside off, pushed towards point for a single.
Full and fired on middle, defended in front of short leg.
This is wider outside off, not played at.
Outside off, left alone.
That is a lovely shot but a wonderful stop. Full and wide outside off, Lokesh drives it through the covers but Rajindra Chandrika dives to his left to stop the ball.
Full and around off, Rahul defends it towards covers.
Full again, driven straight to mid off this time.
Full and straight, Rahul drives it through mid on but short mid-wicket gets across to his left to stop.
Goes back and works it behind square leg.
Shorter in length, Pujara goes back and works it towards square leg.
Comes down the track and drives it straight down the ground but Chase dives to his right and makes a half-stop.
Outside off, watchfully defended.
Slightly shorter of full length, tucked uppishly over mid-wicket for a single. Moves to 70 from 86 balls.

Full and on middle, Rahul gets down and across and gently paddles it through fine leg. The heavy outfield does not allow the ball to get to the boundary and Marlon Samuels gets to it from short fine leg. Two runs taken.
Short of a length outside off, Pujara has no interest in playing at that.
Landed outside off, left alone.
Short and outside off, Pujara taps it to the off side.
Just for information sake, we are into the extra half an hour. 10 overs remaining after this, doubt whether we will get all in.
Pushes this towards mid on.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
Outside off, Rahul turns it through square leg for a couple. The stand moves to 21 from 39 balls. The deficit is now down to 88.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Full and outside off, defended to the off side.
More flight outside off, Cheteshwar defends it watchfully.
Tossed up on middle, Pujara comes down the track and defends it.
Landed outside off, spinning in, Rahul watches it carefully and plays it with the turn to the leg side for a single.
Outside off, left alone.
Full and outside off, Rahul pushes it towards extra covers and takes a quick single.
Full and outside off, Rahul leans and pushes it towards backward point.
Around off, defended in front of short extra cover.
Wide outside off, not played at. Don't think he has the pace to bowl that length.
Back of a length around off, defended back to the bowler.
HOLDER back on.
Once again, Cheteshwar comes down the track and defends.
FOUR! Gets it this time! Pujara has been itching to come down the track and get the gap and this time he drives it through the covers for a boundary. 100 IS UP FOR INDIA.
Comes down the track and flicks it straight to short mid-wicket.
Similar ball, this time Lokesh smartly maneuvers it wide of mid on for a single.
Fuller, draws the batsman forward who obliges and defends.
Landed outside off, spinning in, extra bounce, Rahul goes back and keeps it down.
A wasted ball, short and wide outside off, left alone.
Back of a length around off, Cheteshwar taps it to the off side, sets off for a run but then immediately says "NO!"
A bouncer down the leg side, Pujara ducks.

Slants this down the leg side, tucked towards fine leg for a single. Leg bye signalled. It is a 140 kph ball according to the TV feed. Still, don't know how the ball went that far to fine leg if it it did not hit the bat.
On middle and off, defended back to the bowler.

FOUR! Not a bad line but a good shot. Outside off, on a good length, Rahul just opens the face of the bat and guides it through backward point for a boundary. In total control. The deficit is now down to double digits. Rahul moves to 62 with his 10th boundary. The stand moves to 10 from 16 balls.
Full and outside off, Cheteshwar comes down the track and almost yorks himself. Digs it back to the bowler.
Outside off, worked straight to short mid-wicket.
Makes full use of his height, releases the ball at a high point over his head, puts this outside off and Pujara defends.
Outside off, pushed towards deepish mid on for one.
Plays the slog sweep through mid-wicket for a run.
Full and outside off, swept uppishly to deep mid-wicket for a single.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Full on off, Pujara drives it straight back to the bowler who mimes a shy at the stumps at the striker's end.
Stays back in his crease and defends it towards point.

Ooohh... that was a bit uppish. On a good length outside off, Rahul looks to push it away but the extra bounce catches him off guard. He ends up fending at it and the ball goes off the outside edge through gully. Gets a run.
Goes back and tucks it through square leg for a single.
Landed outside off, defended towards point.
CUMMINS back on.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended. Just a run and a wicket from the over, Chase has figures of 3-1-7-1.
Down the leg side, spinning away, Rahul looks to tuck it away but misses. The bat was very close to the ball there. Almost nicked it.
Off the mark first ball. Pujara goes back and tucks this through square leg for a single.
CHETESHWAR PUJARA to bat next.

OUT! Stop the press. West Indies have taken a wicket. Dhawan departs cheaply. This is well tossed up outside off, Dhawan looks to drive but does not bother to keep it down. The ball goes towards short extra cover where Darren Bravo takes it this time. Dhawan departs for a watchful 27 and the 87-run stand has been broken. Chase has his first victim in Tests. India trail by 109 runs.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full and wide outside off, Dhawan looks to drive but gets a thick outside edge which does not carry to point.
Short and outside off, punched straight to cover.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Goes back and works it through backward square leg for a couple. The deficit is now down to 109.
A long hop, pulled to deep mid-wicket where substitute Leon Johnson gets to his right and slides to save the boundary. That was hit so well that the batsmen took only a single.
FOUR! Up and over! Don't think he middled it though. Charges down the track, is not quite to the pitch of the tossed up ball but goes through with his shot and just clears mid on.
A short ball on middle, Rahul goes back and pulls it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Outside off, allowed to go through.
Ooohh... this is uppish but does not carry. Dhawan looks to drive but fails to keep it down. The ball lands just short of mid off.
Full and outside off, driven towards cover again.
Full on middle, pushed towards covers.
Outside off, pushed towards point.
Short and outside off, Dhawan looks to cut but gets a bottom edge.
Full and outside off, pushed straight to cover.
Stays back in his crease and blocks.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman.
Short and outside off, Rahul looks to cut but gets a bottom edge.

FOUR! MAIDEN TEST FIFTY! Well played. The last two times he has reached a half century, he has eradicated that half and gone on to make a full century. A long hop on middle, Rahul goes back and pulls it behind square leg for a boundary. The deficit is now 117. His conversion rate is good... a lovely chance to maintain the same.
A short ball on middle, Dhawan goes back and pulls it through mid-wicket for a single.
DEVENDRA BISHOO has finally come on to bowl.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
On middle, flicked away for a couple.

DROPPED! Loose from Rahul. It is that time of the day when batsmen slowly start to lose focus. Rahul is perhaps wanting to unsettle the spinner, hence trying a few shots. He swings hard at this one and the ball goes off the inner half of the bat towards short mid-wicket where Darren Bravo sticks out of his left hand but the ball does not stick.
Down the leg side, Rahul misses his flick as the ball spins away.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
FOUR! Welcome into the attack! Full and outside off, Rahul lofts this with ease and gets it over mid-wicket for a boundary!
ROSTON CHASE to roll his arms.
The batsman has driven it straight down the ground.
On middle, worked through square leg for a single.
The batsman has dug out that yorker at the last second.
FOUR! Lovely shot. Short and outside off, Rahul cuts it behind point and gets a boundary. The deficit is now down to 129.
FOUR BYES! Full and down the leg side, swings further down, Rahul looks to flick but misses. An athletic Shane Dowrich dives to his left but cannot get there.
A short ball around off, extra bounce as Cummins bangs it hard, Rahul jumps to fend but gets a thick inside edge onto his pads.
CUMMINS back on.

Drinks are on the field. The Indian openers have played well and the score is 59/0 now. They trail by 137 runs. West Indies have bowled decent lines but haven't got any rewards. It will be interesting to see how and when they will bring spin into action.
Length ball on middle and off, Dhawan gets cramped and blocks it into the ground.
Hurls it fuller on the pads, a play and a miss. The ball hits the pads.
Fuller ball on leg stump line. Dhawan stays tall and plays it to the leg side.
Back of a length ball on off, Rahul goes off his back foot and punches it through covers for a single.
No ball. Fuller ball on middle and leg, Rahul blocks it into the ground. No ball for overstepping.
Length ball on off, cut to point.
Hurls a length ball on off, it goes straight after pitching. Rahul looks to defend but it goes off the outside edge through gully. Brace taken.
FOUR! Another drive! loose ball on off, Dhawan who is well set now launches it through covers. The ball reaches the fence in no time.
On the pads, played to the leg side.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
FOUR! Driven! Tad fuller on off, Dhawan gets to the pitch of the ball and drives it with ease through covers for a boundary. With that 50-run stand is up.
Full ball on middle and leg, Dhawan pushes it back to the bowler.
Holder angles in from around the wickets. Dhawan tucks it to square leg.
Full ball on middle and leg, it goes off the thigh pad to the leg side.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Back of a length ball on off, Rahul goes back and fends it to point.
Edged and safe! Full ball on off, Dhawan goes for a push and it goes of the edge towards first slip. It falls just short and beats Darren Bravo. Single taken.
Too full and wide outside off, a play and a miss.
Full ball on off, Dhawan tries to flick it to the leg side but it goes off the leading edge to mid off.
Once again, the age old sightscreen issue continues... Gabriel comes running and Dhawan stops him. Shannon is frustrated with that.
Full on middle and leg, Rahul pushes it back to the bowler.
Full ball on off, played to covers.
A good length ball outside off, it bounces off the deck a bit more, a play and a miss.
Hurls a length ball wide outside off, left alone.
FOUR! Superbly driven! Tad full, width on offer. Rahul off his front foot elegantly drives it through covers. He is picking his spots quite well here.
Length ball on off, it angles in after pitching. Rahul gets forward and turns it down to the leg side.
Tad full on off, a solid defense by Dhawan off his back foot to the off side.
Length ball outside off, Dhawan is not bothered and leaves it for the keeper.
Dhawan pulls off just when Gabriel was about to bowl. Some sightscreen issue there. The delay continues as the issue is still not sorted.
The batsman just manages to keep the yorker out. Good ball bowled by the bowler.
Hurls a length ball outside off, Dhawan leaves it for the keeper.
Tad short on off, Dhawan off his back foot cuts it to point.
Fuller ball on off, pushed to wide of mid off. Cummins comes running from mid off and makes a good stop.
GABRIEL back on.
On the pads, played to the leg side for a single. India trail by 154.
Tad fuller ball on off, driven by Rahul through covers. Brace was on but the overthrow perhaps a wayward throw makes it three runs in total.
Fuller ball on the pads, Dhawan looks to flick to short fine leg and gets it off his pads. Single taken.
A good length ball on off, a good leave by Dhawan as that ball shaped away.
Tad fuller ball on off, Shikhar pushes it to covers.
Holder bowls a good length ball on off, it angles away from the southpaw. Dhawan lets it through.
Hurls a length ball wide outside off, left alone.
FOUR! Two in two! Short ball on middle and leg, Rahul pulls it to long leg for another boundary. This lad can play shots all around the park.
FOUR! Superb! Full ball on off, Rahul strides forward and punches it through covers for a well placed boundary.
Tad full ball on off, it held its line. Another leave from KL Rahul.
Full ball on off, it angles away after pitching. Rahul leaves it for the keeper.
Hurls a length ball wide outside off, Rahul shoulders his arms.
Length ball on off, pushed to covers.
A perfect length ball on off, it held its line after pitching. Dhawan taps it to covers and looks to run it across but decides against it.
A perfect ball outside off, left alone.
Back of a length ball on off, angling away. Dhawan steers it to point.
FOUR! Tad short and outside off. Dhawan cuts it nicely through backward point for a boundary.
Length ball outside off, left alone.
JASON HOLDER will bowl next.
Tad full on middle, flicked to the leg side.
FOUR! Classic shot! Full on middle and leg, Rahul uses the full face of the bat and punches it down the ground for a boundary.
FOUR! Driven! Tad full outside off, Rahul uses the width and drives it through covers for a boundary. Easy pickings for KL Rahul that.
Length ball on middle and leg, Rahul tucks it to the leg side.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends it from his crease.
A short ball around off, Rahul sways away.
Hurls a length ball outside off, a play and a miss.
FOUR! Cut away! Tad short ball outside off, Dhawan off his back foot cuts it over backward point for a boundary. Good placement there by the southpaw.
Tad fuller ball on middle and leg, Rahul off his front foot pushes it through mid on. Samuels puts in a chase and saves a run for his side. Three runs taken.
Length ball outside off, left alone.
Full ball on the leg side, Rahul goes after it but still misses.
Gabriel angles in a length ball from wide of the crease. Rahul blocks it to the leg side.
Length ball on middle and leg, Dhawan stays back in his crease. The ball nips back in and hits him on his thigh pad. End of over.
Full on off, pushed to mid off.
The batsman defends it from within the crease. They pick up a single.
Back of a length ball outside off, it bounces a bit. Rahul plays it away from his body to point.
Classic shot! Full ball outside off, Rahul gets to the pitch of the ball and hits it through covers. The ball slows down just before the ropes and only a brace is taken.
Tad fuller on middle and leg, Rahul stays back and chips to the leg side.
Back of a length ball on off, Dhawan gets cramped for room and pushes it to covers.
Full in the slot for Rahul. He drills it to covers for a single.
A perfect length in the area of uncertainty. A play and miss by Rahul.
Short and down the leg side. Rahul ducks in to let that go back to the keeper.
Tad fuller on middle and leg, Rahul moves across and tucks it to mid-wicket.
Short and wide outside off, Dhawan taps it to point for a single.
A good length ball on off, Rahul sets back and fends it to point. Well placed by opener.
Peach! Length ball on off, it shapes away from KL Rahul off his back foot poke.
Fuller ball on off, pushed to covers via inside edge off pads for a single. Dhawan gets underway with that.
A full ball on off, angles away. Shikhar leaves it to see the ball thud into the gloves of the keeper.
Short and wide outside off, Dhawan tries to play at it but lets it through.
Hurls a length ball outside off, Dhawan lets it through.
MIGUEL CUMMINS will bowl from the other end.
Length ball on off, it angles in after pitching. Rahul comes forward and tries to block it. The ball strikes the pads and LBW appeal is turned down. The impact was clearly outside off.
Bouncer! Short on middle and leg, it bounces a bit less and Rahul ducks in time to let that go.
Beaten! Full ball outside off, Rahul looks to block that but gets beaten.
Length ball on off, angles in. KL Rahul comes forward and defends it of the front foot to covers.
FOUR! Off the mark! Half-volley on middle and leg, KL Rahul sets himself back and pushes it elegantly through the vacant mid on region for a boundary.
Gabriel steams in and bowls a full ball on off, KL Rahul blocks it off his front foot.
